title: Defendants Charged in First Wave of Housing Stabilization Fraud Cases

supports: Eight defendants were federally charged with wire fraud for roles in the Housing Stabilization Services (HSS) fraud scheme, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson on September 18, 2025.

The release states Minnesota's HSS program, dating to July 2022, made Minnesota the first state to offer Medicaid coverage for Housing Stabilization Services, intended to help people with disabilities, seniors, and people with mental illness or substance-use disorders find and maintain housing.
The release states HSS covered four service types: housing consultation, housing transition services, housing sustaining services, and moving expenses.

The release states the Program was projected to cost about $2.6 million annually before its first year, but actual payouts were $21 million (2021), $42 million (2022), $74 million (2023), $104 million (2024), and $61 million in just the first six months of 2025.
The release attributes the program's vulnerability to low barriers to entry for providers and beneficiaries and minimal reimbursement documentation requirements.
Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson is quoted: 'What we see are schemes stacked upon schemes, draining resources meant for those in need... The fraud must be stopped.'
